lumbright.name: Lumbright
lumbright.lore: Where every adventurer's tale begins. A sleepy river town under an old castle, ringed by cabbage fields and the gentlest monsters in Eldermoor.

varrick.name: Varrick
varrick.lore: The great stone capital — crowded markets, the grand smithy, and roads that run to every corner of Eldermoor.

faloden.name: Faloden
faloden.lore: A walled city of knights and miners, its furnaces never cold. The heart of smithing in the west.

ardounne.name: Ardounne
ardounne.lore: A sprawling, divided city of grand spires and crooked back-alleys — paradise for a light-fingered thief.

draynar.name: Draynar
draynar.lore: A quiet village of willows and a watchful bank, just down the river road from Lumbright. Pickpockets practice here before the city.

alkarid.name: Al-Karid
alkarid.lore: A sun-baked toll town at the desert's edge, its great furnace roaring day and night for the caravans.

edgevale.name: Edgevale
edgevale.lore: A rough frontier town on the edge of the lawless north. The bank stays open; the gate stays locked after dark.

barlock.name: Barlock
barlock.lore: A muddy ring of longhouses and anvils where the hill-clans mine, brawl, and hammer iron between feuds.

catherra.name: Catherra
catherra.lore: Nets dry on every fence and the catch is always fresh. A calm coastal village beneath the northern hills.

seerhold.name: Seerhold
seerhold.lore: A misty town of soothsayers and flax fields, where the crystal halls hum with quiet magic.

brimhollow.name: Brimhollow
brimhollow.sub: Tropical port of the south isle
brimhollow.lore: A humid harbour town under a smoking volcano, all dock-rats, rum, and ships bound for stranger shores.

canifel.name: Canifel
canifel.lore: A shuttered village in the eastern marsh, where the fog never lifts and something always watches the road.

camlann.name: Camlann
camlann.lore: A noble hill-town of banners and knights-errant, the northernmost seat of honour in Eldermoor.

portsarin.name: Port Sarin
portsarin.lore: A salt-crusted harbour town of fishmongers and smugglers, where every ship south casts off from its crowded quays.
